language_wrapper: On a {n}×{n} chessboard, place m standard 1×2 dominoes so that every placed domino is jammed: no domino can slide along its own axis when all other dominoes remain fixed. Among all such jammed configurations on this {n}×{n} board (with at least one domino placed), determine the minimal possible value of m.
hardness_rationale: The seed asks for the minimal jammed count on a fixed 7×7 board. Our family extends to arbitrary odd n ≥ 7 and requires understanding a global blocking strategy and a tight counting lower bound for jammed configurations. The lower bound comes from pairing endpoints and the impossibility of simultaneously freeing a domino end without creating additional slack elsewhere; the constructive upper bound for odd n relies on a non-trivial bracing pattern that leaves exactly five strategic empty cells while immobilizing all dominoes. Solving any instance demands a generalized, board-size-aware argument rather than a single-case construction, thus significantly increasing difficulty.
notes: Instances are restricted to odd n ≥ 7 to avoid edge-pathological cases where corner effects trivialize jamming or fail the bracing pattern. The verifier encodes the derived closed-form; future maintainers can augment with a construction checker if necessary.
source_question: Place \(m\) \(1 \times 2\) dominos on a \(7\times7\) chessboard such that no domino can slide horizontally or vertically when other dominos remains fixed. Find the minimal possible value of \(m\).
